title: Paranormal expert breaks down the most haunted places in Greater Manchester
excerpt: From pint glasses flying off tables in a Wigan pub to the famous rotating Egyptian statue in Manchester Museum, paranormal author Peter Naldrett reveals the chilling history behind Greater Manchester's most haunted spots.
content:
A paranormal expert has broken down the most haunted places in Greater Manchester.

Having previously taken on the UK’s coasts and islands, Peter Naldrett’s latest book Spooky Britain, takes readers on a thrilling tour of the UK’s most haunted houses, sinister dungeons and mysterious crypts. Peter explains the origins of everything from eerie pubs and creepy museums to legendary sites steeped in witchcraft and vampiric lore.

Offering practical tips for those who want to experience the supernatural for themselves, it's an essential read for ghost-hunters and thrill-seekers. With 100 destinations featured, Peter revealed why he was interested in writing the book.

“I have a background in travel writing. I'm always interested in the next idea. When you’re taking on a book project that will take you a couple of years, it’s got to be something you’re interested in. Something that really takes your attention. The paranormal has always interested me.

“When I was a student, just up the road from Lancashire, I basically lived in a haunted house where a number of strange things happened. In 2024, we were in the Paris Catacombs with thousands of skulls. I was reading a book about dark tourism around the world, I thought there hasn’t been a book written about this in a long time.

“I grew up in the 80s with compendium ghost books and you’d see stories that would terrify you as a kid. This is one of those books, it doesn’t focus on one particular paranormal genre, it tries to pull everything together. There’s places that are fun and places that are for serious ghost hunters only,” he said.

Peter added: “I thought it was ambitious trying to get 100 chapters, it was nowhere near enough. It would easily accommodate a follow up book… Britain is good for this kind of thing because we love telling stories.

“We love passing these tales on and we have such a long and often gruesome history. Practically every settlement and every place has a ghost story.”

With Saturday (October 31) marking Halloween, Peter spoke to the Manchester Evening News about some of the spooky Greater Manchester areas you can find in his book.

Delph Tavern

"Delph Tavern in Wigan is a hot spot of pub ghost tourism. It does have several sightings linked to things that have happened there. There’s meant to be a woman in a Victorian dress at the back of the pub and the wife of a quarryman. People have experienced cold spots and there’s the thing that has been captured by CCTV of glasses moving, coming off the table and smashing at the bottom.

"The Delph Tavern is unusual in that it does have a few occurrences that have been photographed. There’s CCTV footage on YouTube and Tiktok. I think haunted pubs are a genre of their own really. There’s many pubs that claim to be the most haunted, I don’t think one particular pub can claim that. There are certainly, the Delph Tavern among them, pub buildings where it's so ingrained in its character that you’d have to be very confident in your skepticism to say there’s nothing there.

“Pubs are interesting because it also depends on the landlord. There have been pubs with a ghostly reputation and a new landlord will take over and wants nothing to do with that. They shut it down, don’t advertise it and don’t invite ghost hunters in for ghost hunting night. You’ve got to have the reputation and a landlord who's open to it,” Peter said.

Manc

“It’s not massively well publicised as a tourist attraction. We first went there because my kids were doing the Egyptians at school and heard that they had good artefacts there. Then learnt the story of the Neb-Sanu statue, which is said to turn on its axis inside its display case.

“There’s a rational explanation, which is the vibrations outside. I quite like the fact that there’s a rational explanation, but we don’t know for definite. It could be linked with all the famous Egyptian curses. I like that element of mystery and that it’s so accessible for people to see.

“This caused a bit of a media storm in 2013, I love when there’s a paranormal debate that enters the media. That was when they realised that it was spinning and it got in some newspapers. Professor Brian Cox waded in on it. It was a fun little mystery,” Peter said.

All Saints Burial Ground

“It’s really interesting that a lot of the people who use it are students who don’t know the history of Manchester. If you don’t read the plaque, you wouldn’t be aware of its background. What happened in Victorian times all over the country is that the death rate was so high that these places got crowded very quickly. People got buried in small places and on top of each other.

“These places in some instances had almost 10,000 people buried in such a small place. When you have the knowledge of that, it makes it a very creepy place. There’s been cases of people having strange experiences in these mass graveyards,” Peter said.

Smithills Hall

“The hall itself was built on top of a mediaeval cemetery, that’s just asking for trouble. As soon as I found that out my thoughts went to Poltergeist. If you’re inviting ghosts into your home, that’s the place you’d want to build it.

“There’s lots of hauntings that have been suspected there. One of the great things is that you can do ghost hunt evenings. There’s companies where you’re invited in and given all of the recording equipment, then spend the evening ghost hunting.

“If you walk around a place like that, it’s creepy enough and you can tell how certain places can be haunted. If you’re there after dark with a team, I think that it will be a very different experience completely.

“Some of the ghosts there include a local farmer who was burned at the stake for being a protestant. We’ve had sightings of people in the chapel who were on their knees praying. Some people have heard horses' hooves galloping on the ground when there aren’t any horses about,” Peter said.

Spooky Britain is out now
